subject: Political Science (Code: 323)
past_paper_reference: CUET UG Political Science Past Papers (2022-2024)

questions.question: Which public sector enterprise in Karnataka manufactures the specialized indelible ink used to mark voters' fingers in Indian general elections?
options: A) Mysore Paints and Varnish Limited
B) Hindustan Antibiotics Limited
C) Bharat Heavy Electricals Limited
D) National Chemical Laboratory
questions.explanation: Mysore Paints and Varnish Limited, a Karnataka government undertaking established in 1937, holds the exclusive license to manufacture indelible voter ink for Indian elections.

questions.question: What provisional government was formed in Bombay in 1947 by citizens of Junagadh to liberate the state from its pro-Pakistan Nawab?
options: A) Azad Hind Fauj
B) Arzi Hukumat (led by Samaldas Gandhi)
C) Mukti Morcha
D) Praja Mandal Provisional Council
questions.explanation: The people of Junagadh formed a provisional government called the 'Arzi Hukumat' headed by Samaldas Gandhi in Bombay to resist the Nawab's accession to Pakistan.

questions.question: The National Dairy Development Board (NDDB) was established in 1965 with its headquarters located in which town of Gujarat?
options: A) Ahmedabad
B) Surat
C) Anand
D) Vadodara
questions.explanation: The National Dairy Development Board (NDDB) was set up in 1965 under the leadership of Dr. Verghese Kurien in Anand, Gujarat, to replicate the Amul cooperative model nationwide.

questions.question: Where was the historic Asian Relations Conference held in March 1947 under Jawaharlal Nehru's visionary leadership, five months before Indian independence?
options: A) Bandung
B) Colombo
C) Rangoon
D) New Delhi
questions.explanation: Nehru convened the Asian Relations Conference in New Delhi in March 1947, bringing together representatives from across Asia to assert post-colonial solidarity.

questions.sub_topic: Challenge to and Restoration of Congress System
questions.question: Which political term was coined to describe the unstable state governments formed in several northern Indian states following the 1967 elections, consisting of multiple ideologically conflicting parties?
options: A) Coalition Governments (Samyukta Vidhayak Dal)
B) Unitary Presidential Directorates
C) All-India Socialist Communes
D) Autonomous Zonal Councils
questions.explanation: The 1967 elections ushered in the era of coalition politics at the state level under the umbrella of Samyukta Vidhayak Dal (SVD) ministries.

questions.question: In which year did the Janata Party government collapse following internal factional rivalries, paving the way for fresh mid-term elections in 1980?
options: A) March 1977
B) July 1979
C) December 1980
D) May 1982
questions.explanation: Prime Minister Morarji Desai resigned in July 1979 after losing the parliamentary majority, and the short-lived Charan Singh government fell within a few months, forcing elections in 1980.

questions.question: Which article of the Indian Constitution, inserted in 1954 via Presidential Order and repealed in 2019, empowered the Jammu and Kashmir legislature to define 'permanent residents' of the state?
options: A) Article 371
B) Article 356
C) Article 35A
D) Article 365
questions.explanation: Article 35A empowered the J&K legislature to confer special rights and privileges on permanent residents regarding state employment, acquisition of immovable property, and scholarships.

questions.sub_topic: Disintegration of the 'Second World' and the Collapse of Bipolarity
questions.question: In which year was the Berlin Wall constructed by the East German communist authorities to prevent citizens from fleeing to West Berlin?
questions.explanation: The Berlin Wall was erected by the German Democratic Republic (East Germany) in August 1961, physically dividing the city until its fall on 9 November 1989.

questions.sub_topic: Alternative Centers of Economic and Political Power
questions.question: Which of the following regional economic groupings includes Australia, Canada, Japan, South Korea, the United States, and several Pacific Rim nations?
options: A) Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC)
B) European Union (EU)
C) SAARC
D) OPEC
questions.explanation: APEC was founded in 1989 to promote sustainable economic growth and free trade among Pacific Rim member economies, including the US, Japan, China, and Australia.

questions.sub_topic: International Organisations in a Unipolar World
questions.question: Who was the first Secretary-General of the United Nations, serving from 1946 to 1952?
options: A) Dag Hammarskjold of Sweden
B) Trygve Lie of Norway
C) U Thant of Burma
D) Kurt Waldheim of Austria
questions.explanation: Norwegian politician and diplomat Trygve Lie served as the first elected Secretary-General of the United Nations from February 1946 until his resignation in November 1952.

questions.question: Why did the Congress Party in the 1950s function as what political scientists called a 'coalition of factions'?
options: A) Because it was legally compelled by the Supreme Court to share ministries with the Jana Sangh
B) Because all party decisions were made by a hereditary council of royal princely patrons
C) Because it accommodated competing regional, social, and ideological factions within the party, acting as both the ruling party and its own internal opposition
D) Because the Communist Party held a controlling veto on all internal party appointments
questions.explanation: Congress's internal factions represented different interests and ideologies; internal bargaining between these factions served the role of opposition and maintained equilibrium.

questions.question: Which constitutional provision enacted under the States Reorganisation Act of 1956 instituted statutory Zonal Councils to encourage interstate cooperation?
options: A) The establishment of autonomous military commands in each regional zone
B) The abolition of state legislative assemblies in favor of direct central commissioners
C) The mandatory rotation of state capital cities every five years
D) The creation of five Zonal Councils (Northern, Central, Eastern, Western, and Southern) under the chairmanship of the Union Home Minister
questions.explanation: Part III of the States Reorganisation Act 1956 set up five Zonal Councils headed by the Union Home Minister to foster interstate consultation and settle regional boundary disputes.

questions.question: What structural economic vulnerability did the severe droughts of 1965-1967 expose in India's agricultural development policy?
options: A) The dangerous dependence on foreign food imports under PL-480 and the stagnation of grain yields due to inadequate irrigation and chemical inputs
B) The excessive production of commercial cash crops causing total abandonment of staple cereals
C) The complete collapse of urban banking institutions due to rural over-lending
D) The total failure of the heavy machine-building plants at Ranchi and Bhilai
questions.explanation: The agricultural stagnation and drought of the mid-1960s forced India to rely on foreign food aid with political strings, prompting the decisive pivot towards Green Revolution technologies.

questions.question: What immediate military consequence resulted from the Chinese unilateral ceasefire announced on 21 November 1962 during the Sino-Indian border war?
options: A) Chinese troops permanently annexed the entire state of Assam and Nagaland
B) Chinese forces withdrew 20 kilometers behind the Line of Actual Control (LAC) in the eastern sector, while maintaining control of occupied territory in Aksai Chin
C) China surrendered all claims to Tibet and established diplomatic embassies in Lhasa and Gangtok
D) Indian armed forces took control of all border posts in Xinjiang province
questions.explanation: On 21 November 1962, China declared a unilateral ceasefire and withdrew its troops 20 km behind the line of actual control in NEFA, while retaining its territorial gains in Aksai Chin.

questions.sub_topic: Challenge to and Restoration of Congress System
questions.question: Which constitutional amendment enacted in 1971 restored Parliament's unconditional power to amend any part of the Constitution, including Fundamental Rights, overriding the Golaknath verdict?
options: A) 25th Constitutional Amendment Act
B) 26th Constitutional Amendment Act
C) 24th Constitutional Amendment Act
D) 39th Constitutional Amendment Act
questions.explanation: The 24th Amendment Act of 1971 affirmed that Parliament has the sovereign constituent power under Article 368 to amend any provision of the Constitution, including Part III.

questions.question: What was the official justification given by Prime Minister Indira Gandhi in her national radio broadcast announcing the Emergency on 26 June 1975?
options: A) That Pakistan and China had launched an imminent joint nuclear strike against Indian cities
B) That the Reserve Bank of India had completely exhausted its foreign currency reserves
C) That a catastrophic global pandemic had paralyzed all state healthcare systems
D) That a deep and widespread conspiracy was threatening internal stability, law and order, and normal democratic functioning
questions.explanation: Indira Gandhi stated that democratic institutions were being subverted by opposition agitations, strikes, and JP's incitement of the armed forces, creating an internal emergency.

questions.question: In the post-Emergency elections of March 1977, in which geographic zone of India did the Congress party manage to retain substantial electoral support?
options: A) Southern states (Andhra Pradesh, Karnataka, Kerala, and Tamil Nadu)
B) Northern states (Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, Haryana, and Punjab)
C) Western states (Rajasthan and Gujarat)
D) Eastern states (West Bengal and Odisha)
questions.explanation: While Congress was wiped out across the Hindi heartland in 1977, it won 92 out of 129 seats in the south (Andhra Pradesh and Karnataka especially), where Emergency excesses were less severe.

questions.question: What was the significance of the 1973 Anandpur Sahib Resolution in the evolving discourse on Indian federalism?
options: A) It demanded that Punjab be declared a separate independent sovereign state at the United Nations
B) It articulated a demand for true federalism, proposing that the Centre's jurisdiction be limited to defense, foreign relations, communications, and railways
C) It urged the immediate abolition of all irrigation canal networks linking Punjab and Haryana
D) It called for the merger of Punjab, Haryana, and Himachal Pradesh into a unified sub-nation
questions.explanation: The Anandpur Sahib Resolution asserted that the Centre should retain jurisdiction only over defense, foreign affairs, communications, and currency, with all residual powers given to states.

questions.question: Under the 1985 Assam Accord, what happened to migrants who had entered Assam between 1 January 1966 and 24 March 1971?
options: A) They were immediately deported across the international border within 48 hours
B) They were granted instant unconditional citizenship with guaranteed government jobs
C) They were to be identified and disenfranchised (stripped of voting rights) for a period of 10 years, but permitted to remain
D) They were relocated into special autonomous reservations in neighboring Arunachal Pradesh
questions.explanation: Under the Assam Accord, foreigners entering between 1 Jan 1966 and 24 March 1971 were detected, had their names deleted from electoral rolls for 10 years, after which citizenship was restored.

questions.question: Which prominent leader from Western Uttar Pradesh founded the Bharatiya Kisan Union (BKU) in 1987, leading massive peasant demonstrations at Delhi's Boat Club?
options: A) Choudhary Charan Singh
B) Sharad Joshi
C) Rakesh Tikait
D) Mahendra Singh Tikait
questions.explanation: Mahendra Singh Tikait headed the Bharatiya Kisan Union (BKU), which organized non-party peasant agitations demanding fair electricity tariffs, MSP, and loan waivers in the late 1980s.

questions.question: What was the finding of the Justice Liberhan Commission regarding the demolition of the Babri structure in December 1992?
options: A) That the demolition was not spontaneous, but a meticulously planned and orchestrated operation involving prominent leaders of the Sangh Parivar
B) That the structure had collapsed entirely due to natural geological tremors and foundation decay
C) That the demolition was carried out exclusively by foreign mercenary infiltrators
D) That the state administration of Kalyan Singh had taken every possible military step to prevent the demolition
questions.explanation: The Liberhan Commission report, submitted in 2009 after 17 years, concluded that the demolition was pre-planned and indicted 68 individuals including senior political leaders.

questions.sub_topic: Disintegration of the 'Second World' and the Collapse of Bipolarity
questions.question: What structural role did the 'Nomenklatura' play in the ultimate decay and stagnation of the Soviet political system?
options: A) They were underground capitalist saboteurs funded by the CIA to organize strikes in heavy industries
B) They formed a privileged, entrenched party-bureaucratic elite that enjoyed special perks, resisted reforms, and alienated ordinary citizens
C) They were elected judicial ombudsmen who repeatedly overruled Communist Party executive decrees
D) They were peasant cooperatives that privatized grain distribution across Soviet collective farms
questions.explanation: The Nomenklatura was the bureaucratic oligarchy that controlled state apparatus, enjoyed luxury stores and dachas, stifled efficiency, and generated widespread public cynicism.

questions.sub_topic: Disintegration of the 'Second World' and the Collapse of Bipolarity
questions.question: Which post-communist republic in Eastern Europe witnessed a violent, bloody overthrow and execution of its dictator Nicolae Ceausescu on Christmas Day 1989?
options: A) Poland
B) Hungary
C) Romania
D) Bulgaria
questions.explanation: Romania was the only Eastern European state where the fall of communism was violent; a popular revolt led to the capture and execution of Nicolae and Elena Ceausescu on 25 December 1989.

questions.sub_topic: Alternative Centers of Economic and Political Power
questions.question: What is the primary function of the Council of the European Union (also known as the Council of Ministers)?
options: A) It commands the tactical nuclear submarine fleet of the European continent
B) It serves as the supreme appellate court for criminal homicide cases across Western Europe
C) It prints physical euro notes and sets commercial retail lending rates in Frankfurt
D) It represents the national governments of EU member states and negotiates and adopts EU laws jointly with the European Parliament
questions.explanation: The Council of the European Union represents member states' governments, gathering national ministers by policy area to adopt legislation and coordinate EU policies.

questions.sub_topic: Alternative Centers of Economic and Political Power
questions.question: Which South Korean policy initiative of the late 1990s sought peaceful engagement and reconciliation with North Korea?
options: A) The Sunshine Policy (initiated by President Kim Dae-jung)
B) The Han River Accord
C) The Seoul Security Doctrine
D) The Demilitarized Zone Protocol
questions.explanation: President Kim Dae-jung launched the 'Sunshine Policy' in 1998, emphasizing economic cooperation and family reunions, for which he was awarded the 2000 Nobel Peace Prize.

questions.sub_topic: South Asia in the Post Cold War Era
questions.question: What was the tragic incident in June 2001 that decimated the royal family of Nepal and deepened the political crisis in the country?
options: A) The Maoist storming of the Singha Durbar secretariat
B) The Royal Palace Massacre at Narayanhiti Palace in Kathmandu
C) The assassination of King Mahendra during a border inspection
D) The bombing of the Pashupatinath temple during a state festival
questions.explanation: Crown Prince Dipendra shot and killed King Birendra, Queen Aishwarya, and seven other royal family members at Narayanhiti Palace on 1 June 2001 before shooting himself.

questions.sub_topic: International Organisations in a Unipolar World
questions.question: What was the primary argument advanced by India in favor of reforming and restructuring the United Nations Security Council?
options: A) That the United Nations should be dissolved and replaced with a military alliance of Asian nations
B) That permanent membership should be granted exclusively to countries with nuclear submarines
C) That the UNSC reflects the geopolitical reality of 1945 and lacks equitable geographic representation from developing countries like India
D) That the UN headquarters should be permanently relocated from New York to Geneva
questions.explanation: India argues that the UNSC's current composition reflects obsolete 1945 power dynamics and excludes major developing democracies representing massive populations and economic power.

questions.question: What is meant by the strategic concept of 'Deterrence' in traditional security studies?
options: A) Surrendering sovereign border territory in exchange for temporary trade concessions
B) Dismantling all conventional armed forces to foster mutual international trust
C) Conducting continuous military invasions to eliminate all foreign governments
D) Preventing an adversary from initiating war by threatening unacceptable damage in retaliation
questions.explanation: Deterrence is the military strategy where a state demonstrates sufficient retaliatory force to convince a potential aggressor that the costs of an attack will drastically exceed any gains.

questions.sub_topic: Environment and Natural Resources in Global Politics
questions.question: Why did developing nations resist the early environmental proposals pushed by Western countries at the 1992 Earth Summit?
options: A) Because developed nations were historically responsible for the majority of greenhouse emissions, yet sought to impose uniform ecological caps that would stifle third-world industrialisation
B) Because developing nations denied the scientific existence of carbon dioxide in the atmosphere
C) Because developing countries wished to completely deplete all fossil fuel reserves within a decade
D) Because the United Nations Charter prohibits third-world nations from attending ecological summits
questions.explanation: Developing countries argued that developed nations had caused the bulk of ecological damage during centuries of industrialisation and could not impose equal burdens on poor nations seeking poverty alleviation.

questions.question: What is the central argument of left-wing critics of economic globalisation regarding the role of multinational corporations (MNCs)?
options: A) That MNCs force developing nations to nationalise all private property and adopt communist command economies
B) That MNCs exploit cheap labour and lax environmental standards in developing countries, drain local wealth, and widen social inequality
C) That MNCs eliminate international trade in manufactured commodities in favor of barter exchange
D) That MNCs provide excessive wages and welfare benefits that bankrupt local public sector enterprises
questions.explanation: Left critics argue that globalisation benefits wealthy elites and MNCs at the expense of working people, deregulates labour protections, and deepens global socio-economic disparities.

questions.question: Which coalition government formed at the Centre in 1999 under Atal Bihari Vajpayee became the first non-Congress coalition to complete a full five-year term in office?
options: A) United Front
B) National Front
C) National Democratic Alliance (NDA)
D) Janata Morcha
questions.explanation: The National Democratic Alliance (NDA) government headed by Atal Bihari Vajpayee governed from October 1999 to May 2004, completing a full five-year term.

questions.sub_topic: Alternative Centers of Economic and Political Power
questions.question: Which of the following treaty revisions signed in 2007 restructured the institutional functioning of the European Union, creating the posts of permanent President of the European Council and High Representative?
options: A) Treaty of Nice
B) Treaty of Amsterdam
C) Single European Act
D) Treaty of Lisbon
questions.explanation: The Treaty of Lisbon (signed 2007, entered into force 2009) reformed EU institutions following the failure of the EU Constitution, establishing a permanent Council President and stronger Parliament.

questions.question: In contemporary security threats, how do 'new wars' waged by non-state transnational terrorist networks differ from classical interstate conflicts?
options: A) They target innocent civilians to generate psychological panic, operate without uniforms across sovereign borders, and are not bound by the Geneva Conventions
B) They involve armored tank divisions clashing exclusively on open desert battlefields
C) They are declared strictly through diplomatic ultimatums presented to the UN Security Council
D) They observe strict reciprocal prisoner-of-war exchange treaties supervised by the Red Cross
questions.explanation: Transnational terrorism uses asymmetric tactics, deliberately targeting non-combatant civilians to spread terror, operating through decentralized cells across international boundaries.

questions.question: Which distinguished jurist and parliamentarian served as Law Minister in Nehru's post-independence cabinet before resigning in September 1951 over the shelving of the Hindu Code Bill?
options: A) Alladi Krishnaswami Iyer
B) Dr. B.R. Ambedkar
C) K.M. Munshi
D) N. Gopalaswami Ayyangar
questions.explanation: Dr. B.R. Ambedkar resigned as Law Minister in September 1951, frustrated by the Cabinet's hesitation and conservative opposition to passing the progressive Hindu Code Bill.

questions.question: What was the administrative formula adopted in the Official Languages Act of 1963 regarding the continued use of English after the expiry of the initial 15-year constitutional transition period in 1965?
options: A) English was immediately abolished and all central government offices were required to use Hindi exclusively from 26 January 1965
B) English was declared the sole national language of India for the next 50 years
C) English 'may' continue to be used in addition to Hindi for all official purposes of the Union and in Parliament
D) All non-Hindi speaking states were placed under direct presidential commissioners until they adopted Hindi
questions.explanation: Section 3 of the Official Languages Act 1963 provided that English 'may' continue to be used alongside Hindi, which was later strengthened in 1967 following anti-Hindi protests in Tamil Nadu.

questions.question: Which of the following describes the key theoretical insight of the 'Feldman-Mahalanobis Strategy' adopted during the Second Five Year Plan?
options: A) Maximizing the export of raw agricultural cotton to finance consumer electronics manufacturing
B) Directing 90% of all public investments into rural handicrafts and decentralized handloom cooperatives
C) Abolishing all protective tariffs to encourage cheap industrial imports from developed nations
D) Prioritizing the domestic manufacture of capital goods (machines to make machines) to permanently break dependence on foreign industrial imports
questions.explanation: The Mahalanobis model posited that building up heavy capital goods industries (steel, heavy engineering) was essential to accelerate the long-term rate of domestic capital accumulation.

questions.question: Which boundary protocol negotiated in 1954 between India and China contained the preamble that first formulated the Five Principles of Peaceful Coexistence (Panchsheel)?
options: A) Agreement on Trade and Intercourse between Tibet Region of China and India
B) Simla Convention on Border Demarcation
C) Beijing Friendship and Mutual Assistance Treaty
D) New Delhi Consular Agreement on Aksai Chin
questions.explanation: The preamble to the 1954 Sino-Indian Agreement on Trade and Intercourse between the Tibet Region of China and India contained the five principles of Panchsheel.

questions.sub_topic: Challenge to and Restoration of Congress System
questions.question: Which constitutional amendment bill to abolish the Privy Purses failed by just one-third of a vote in the Rajya Sabha in September 1970, prompting Indira Gandhi to de-recognize the princes via Presidential Order?
options: A) 21st Constitutional Amendment Bill
B) 24th Constitutional Amendment Bill (1970)
C) 29th Constitutional Amendment Bill
D) 32nd Constitutional Amendment Bill
questions.explanation: When the Privy Purse abolition bill failed to achieve a two-thirds majority in the Rajya Sabha by a single vote, Indira Gandhi issued a Presidential Order de-recognizing the rulers, which the Supreme Court struck down in Madhav Rao Scindia (1970).

questions.question: In the habeas corpus case of ADM Jabalpur (1976), who was the Attorney General of India who argued on behalf of the Union Government that during an emergency, a citizen could not complain even if life was taken without the sanction of law?
options: A) C.K. Daphtary
B) K. Parasaran
C) Niren De
D) Soli Sorabjee
questions.explanation: Attorney General Niren De argued that in view of the Presidential Order under Article 359, even arbitrary deprivation of personal liberty or life was beyond the scrutiny of writ courts.

questions.question: Which prominent moderate Akali leader who signed the 1985 Punjab Accord with Prime Minister Rajiv Gandhi was assassinated by Sikh extremists less than a month later in August 1985?
options: A) Jathedar Gurcharan Singh Tohra
B) Surjit Singh Barnala
C) Balwant Singh
D) Sant Harchand Singh Longowal
questions.explanation: Sant Harchand Singh Longowal was shot dead at a gurdwara in Sherpur on 20 August 1985, barely four weeks after signing the Punjab Accord, demonstrating the violent backlash from extremists.

questions.question: In which state did the Bahujan Samaj Party (BSP) form a historic coalition government in June 1995 with outside support from the BJP, making Mayawati the first Dalit woman Chief Minister in India?
options: A) Uttar Pradesh
B) Madhya Pradesh
C) Bihar
D) Rajasthan
questions.explanation: On 3 June 1995, Mayawati was sworn in as the Chief Minister of Uttar Pradesh at the head of a short-lived BSP minority government supported externally by the BJP.

questions.question: In the aftermath of the 2002 Gujarat communal violence, which statutory national body intervened decisively before the Supreme Court, seeking retrials outside the state and protection of witnesses in cases like Best Bakery?
options: A) National Commission for Minorities
B) National Human Rights Commission (NHRC)
C) Law Commission of India
D) Central Vigilance Commission
questions.explanation: The NHRC, headed by former CJI J.S. Verma, intervened proactively, documenting state complicity and moving the Supreme Court to transfer sensitive cases (like Best Bakery and Bilkis Bano) to Maharashtra for fair trials.

questions.sub_topic: Disintegration of the 'Second World' and the Collapse of Bipolarity
questions.question: Under the New Union Treaty (Novo-Ogaryovo process) negotiated by Gorbachev in early 1991, what restructuring of the Soviet Union was proposed before being derailed by the August coup?
options: A) The total abolition of all republic governments in favor of direct central military rule from Moscow
B) The immediate merger of the Soviet Union with the European Economic Community
C) A decentralized federation of sovereign republics sharing common defense, foreign policy, and currency, voluntarily signed by the republics
D) The partitioning of the USSR into 50 autonomous capitalist provinces owned by Western banks
questions.explanation: Gorbachev's proposed New Union Treaty aimed to transform the USSR into a genuine voluntary federation of sovereign republics; hardliners staged the August 1991 coup the day before it was scheduled to be signed.

questions.sub_topic: Alternative Centers of Economic and Political Power
questions.question: What is the specific legal requirement for amending the foundational treaties of the European Union, such as the Treaty on European Union?
options: A) A simple majority vote in the European Parliament with no national ratification needed
B) Approval by the President of the European Central Bank and the Director of the IMF
C) A two-thirds vote among the original six founding members of the EEC
D) Unanimous agreement of all member state governments in an Intergovernmental Conference followed by ratification by every member state according to its constitutional requirements
questions.explanation: Under Article 48 of the Treaty on European Union, ordinary treaty revision procedures require consensus among all member states and unanimous ratification by every national parliament (or via referendum).

questions.sub_topic: South Asia in the Post Cold War Era
questions.question: Under the 1987 Indo-Sri Lanka Accord, which constitutional amendment was enacted by the Sri Lankan Parliament to create Provincial Councils and devolve power to the Tamil-majority Northern and Eastern provinces?
options: A) 13th Amendment to the Sri Lankan Constitution
B) 10th Amendment to the Sri Lankan Constitution
C) 16th Amendment to the Sri Lankan Constitution
D) 18th Amendment to the Sri Lankan Constitution
questions.explanation: Enacted pursuant to the Indo-Sri Lanka Accord in November 1987, the 13th Amendment made Tamil an official language and established Provincial Councils to devolve administrative powers to the provinces.

questions.sub_topic: International Organisations in a Unipolar World
questions.question: Under Article 27(3) of the UN Charter, how has the voting practice of the Security Council evolved regarding an 'abstention' by a permanent member on a substantive resolution?
options: A) An abstention is automatically counted as a negative veto vote that kills the resolution
B) An abstention by a permanent member is not treated as a veto; the resolution passes if it secures the required affirmative votes
C) An abstaining permanent member is suspended from the Security Council for six months
D) Resolutions cannot be voted upon if any permanent member chooses to abstain
questions.explanation: By longstanding diplomatic jurisprudence and practice since 1946, an abstention or voluntary absence by a permanent member is not interpreted as a veto; only an explicit negative vote constitutes a veto.

questions.question: Which landmark bilateral strategic nuclear treaty signed between President Ronald Reagan and Mikhail Gorbachev in December 1987 eliminated an entire class of ground-launched ballistic and cruise missiles with ranges of 500 to 5,500 km?
options: A) Strategic Arms Limitation Treaty I (SALT I)
B) Anti-Ballistic Missile (ABM) Treaty
C) Intermediate-Range Nuclear Forces (INF) Treaty
D) Strategic Offensive Reductions Treaty (SORT)
questions.explanation: The INF Treaty resulted in the verified destruction of 2,692 ground-launched intermediate-range nuclear missiles by the US and USSR, marking a historic breakthrough in Cold War disarmament.

questions.sub_topic: Environment and Natural Resources in Global Politics
questions.question: What is the primary ecological significance of the 1991 Protocol on Environmental Protection to the Antarctic Treaty (Madrid Protocol)?
options: A) It partitions Antarctica into commercial fishing zones allocated to G7 member nations
B) It permits member states to dump treated industrial radioactive waste in the Antarctic ice sheet
C) It allows private cruise liners to build luxury tourist resorts along the Ross Ice Shelf
D) It designates Antarctica as a natural reserve devoted to peace and science, and imposes a comprehensive indefinite ban on commercial mineral resource extraction
questions.explanation: The Madrid Protocol (1991) designates Antarctica as a 'natural reserve, devoted to peace and science' and strictly prohibits all activities relating to Antarctic mineral resources other than scientific research.

questions.question: In the debate on cultural globalisation, what did sociologists mean by the concept of 'Glocalisation'?
options: A) The total erasure of all non-Western languages in favor of English in international diplomacy
B) The simultaneous occurrence of universalising and particularising tendencies, where global products and ideas are actively adapted to local cultural contexts
C) The immediate boycott of all imported consumer goods by sovereign national legislatures
D) The mandatory conversion of local agricultural crops into monoculture exports for Wall Street
questions.explanation: Coined by sociologist Roland Robertson, 'glocalisation' describes how global cultural trends do not simply wipe out local traditions, but interact with them to create unique locally adapted forms.

questions.question: Which of the following describes the radical land reform measure successfully implemented by the Left Front government in West Bengal beginning in 1978 to register and secure the rights of sharecroppers (bargadars)?
options: A) Operation Flood
B) Bhoodan Campaign
C) Intensive Agricultural Scheme
D) Operation Barga
questions.explanation: Operation Barga was a landmark land reform drive launched by the Left Front in West Bengal in 1978 that legally recorded over 1.4 million bargadars (sharecroppers), granting them security against eviction.
